caveats: Ages in age_ma are PBDB interval bounds (coarse stage/NALMA bins) unless noted; see age_notes. Quotes from OCR texts (Black 1963; Emry & Thorington 1982) retain OCR errors.

evidence.quote: Although it is not a Sciurinae, the postcranial skeleton of Douglassciurus is surprisingly similar to that of extant tree squirrels such as Sciurus ( Emry and Thorington, 1982 ; Emry and Thorington, 1984 ), but the archaic protrogomorphous zygomasseteric structure of the skull ( Emry and Korth, 1996 ; Emry and Thorington, 1982 ) is shared with aplodontiids and other primitive rodent groups such as ischyromids. Consequently, Douglassciurus is generally considered the most basal sciurid

notes.age_epoch: middle Eocene (Bartonian; D. oaxacaensis, ~40 Ma) to Oligocene (Whitneyan; D. bjorki, D. sapphirus); type species late Eocene (Chadronian)
notes.age_notes: PBDB genus range: first appearance 41.03-37.71 Ma (Bartonian), last appearance 31.8-29.5 Ma (Rupelian/Whitneyan bin). D. jeffersoni dated 36.6-35.8 Ma (middle Chadronian) by Casanovas-Vilar et al. 2018. Emry & Thorington (1982) called the Chadronian "early Oligocene" (older usage); Chadronian is now late Eocene.
notes.placement_notes: Casanovas-Vilar et al. 2018: "not a Sciurinae", protrogomorphous zygomasseteric structure, most basal sciurid (confirmed by their total-evidence analysis). PBDB classification: Sciuridae (Emry & Korth 2001; Korth et al. 2022), but Korth 2014 (PBDB unselected opinion) placed it in Sciurinae, and Li et al. 2023 list it among Sciurinae in comparisons. Historically referred to Prosciurus (Aplodontidae), Cedromus, and Protosciurus (Emry & Thorington 1982, as Protosciurus jeffersoni). Mercer & Roth 2003 used it to date the base of the crown radiation (per Casanovas-Vilar et al. 2018).
notes.material: Dental material (teeth; D. oaxacaensis known without upper molars) plus a nearly complete skeleton (USNM 243981; palate with maxillary dentition, auditory bullae, skull fragments, both mandibular rami, most of the postcranial skeleton) from Flagstaff Rim, Wyoming. D. oaxacaensis lacks known upper molars.
notes.gliding_evidence: None. The postcranial skeleton is strikingly similar to that of the fox squirrel (Sciurus niger) and was interpreted as that of an arboreal (tree) squirrel; no gliding adaptations reported.

locality.details: USA: Montana (Pipestone Springs, type locality of D. jeffersoni), Wyoming (Flagstaff Rim, skeleton USNM 243981), Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota; Canada: Saskatchewan (Cypress Hills); Mexico: Oaxaca (Yolomecatl, D. oaxacaensis) - per PBDB occurrences and cited papers.

evidence.quote: A new genus of sciurid, Hesperopetes, contains three species: H. thoringtoni (type species), H. jamesi, and H. blacki. H. thoringtoni is from the early Chadronian (late Eocene) White River Formation of central Wyoming and represents the earliest recognized species of sciurid. The other species are from the latest Whitneyan or earliest Arikareean (late Oligocene) Blue Ash local fauna of South Dakota. Hesperopetes is closest in dental morphology to Oligopetes Heissig, which is known only from the early Oligocene of Europe. Hesperopetes may also represent the earliest occurrence of a lineage leading to pteromyine sciurids ("flying" squirrels).
evidence.note: Abstract text obtained through a WebFetch summarisation step (publisher page blocks direct download); appears verbatim but could not be checked against raw text.

evidence.citation: Casanovas-Vilar, I., Garcia-Porta, J., Fortuny, J., Sanisidro, O., Prieto, J., Querejeta, M., Llacer, S., Robles, J.M., Bernardini, F. & Alba, D.M. 2018. Oldest skeleton of a fossil flying squirrel casts new light on the phylogeny of the group. eLife 7:e39270 (full text via Europe PMC PMC6177260)
evidence.quote: Indeed, one of the earliest sciurids, Hesperopetes thoringtoni from the late Eocene (36.6 – 35.8 Ma) of North America, has been related to the lineage leading to flying squirrels according to dental morphology ( Emry and Korth, 2007 ). In the light of molecular results, it was conceded that Hesperopetes unlikely represented a pteromyin and was not assigned to any squirrel subfamily ( Emry and Korth, 2007 ).

evidence.quote: Hesperopetes is last recorded during the earliest Oligocene (Orellan; Korth, 2017 ), coinciding with the oldest record of Sciurion ( Bell, 2004 ), yet another alleged flying squirrel. Isolated cheek teeth are the only material available for all these taxa, which have been related to flying squirrels exclusively based on dental morphology.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, dental features commonly used to recognize flying squirrels are not unique but also present in other sciurids ( Thorington et al., 2005 ), so it is uncertain if any of the extinct ‘flying’ squirrels belonged to this group.

notes.gliding_evidence: None direct. Only dental material is known; the flying-squirrel-like dental features are not diagnostic of gliding (also present in other sciurids). Gliding would require postcranial evidence.

evidence.quote: Palaeosciurus Pomel, 1853 comprises five European species: P. feignouxi (type species), P. fissurae ( Dehm, 1950 ), P. goti ( Vianey-Liaud, 1974 ), P. sutteri ( Ziegler and Fahlbusch, 1986 ), and P. ultimus ( Mein and Ginsburg, 2002 ), and a Chinese species P. jiangi ( Qiu, 2015 ). This genus ranges temporally from the earliest Oligocene to the early Miocene in Eurasia ( de Bruijn, 1999 ; Qiu, 2015 ). Palaeosciurus goti from Mas de Got of France (MP22) was once regarded as the earliest sciurid in Europe ( Vianey-Liaud, 1985 ).

notes.age_epoch: early Oligocene (earliest Oligocene, MP21-22; P. goti) to early Miocene (literature summary) - PBDB records extend into the middle Miocene (MN4-MN5, Langhian; P. sutteri, P. ultimus, P. cf. fissurae)
notes.age_notes: PBDB genus range: first appearance 33.9-27.3 Ma (Rupelian), last appearance 15.98-11.63 Ma (Langhian-Serravallian bin, from P. cf. fissurae, Poland); most youngest records are MN5 (15.98-13.82 Ma). Li et al. 2023 summarise the range as "earliest Oligocene to the early Miocene in Eurasia".
notes.placement_notes: Vianey-Liaud (1974, 1975) described P. goti as a terrestrial squirrel ("ecureuil terrestre") on the basis of limb proportions; Casanovas-Vilar et al. 2018 note it lacks the diagnostic features of any extant group. Li et al. 2023 instead class Palaeosciurus as a tree-squirrel morphotype and list it under Sciurinae. de Bruijn et al. 2013 and PBDB (McKenna & Bell 1997) place it only in Sciuridae. Disagreement therefore exists between "ground squirrel" and "tree squirrel" interpretations.
notes.material: Mostly isolated cheek teeth (e.g. 8 teeth from Banovici); limb bones of P. goti were used by Vianey-Liaud to assess limb proportions (postcranial material therefore exists for at least that species).
notes.gliding_evidence: None. Interpreted as terrestrial from limb proportions (P. goti); no gliding interpretation found in the literature retrieved.

locality.details: Mainly Europe (PBDB occurrences in the listed European countries); Anatolia (Turkey); Kazakhstan (Aral, Late Oligocene, Palaeosciurus sp., PBDB); China (P. jiangi Qiu, 2015, per Li et al. 2023).

evidence.quote: Protosciurus ( Black, 1963 ) includes P. condoni (type species), P. mengi , P. rachelae , and P. tecuyensis ( Bryant, 1945 ). The genus ranges from early Orellan to early Hemingfordian NALMA (early Oligocene to late early Miocene), and it may have survived into the early Barstovian NALMA (early middle Miocene) ( Goodwin, 2008 ).

notes.age_epoch: early Oligocene (early Orellan) to early Miocene (early Hemingfordian), possibly to early middle Miocene (early Barstovian); PBDB also lists Chadronian (late Eocene) records referred to P. cf. mengi / P. mengi
notes.age_notes: PBDB genus range: first appearance 37-33.9 Ma (Priabonian; Chadronian records), last appearance 16.3-12.5 Ma (Early Barstovian, Protosciurus sp., Fleming Fm, Texas). Black 1963 gave "Middle Oligocene of Nebraska, late Oligocene or early Miocene of Oregon, early Miocene of California" (older epoch usage).
notes.placement_notes: Black 1963 placed Protosciurus in tribe Sciurini (with cheek teeth of tree-squirrel type but an incompletely sciuromorphous zygomasseteric structure); PBDB parent = Sciurini (Black 1963), other opinions Sciuridae (McKenna & Bell 1997; Korth et al. 2022). Casanovas-Vilar et al. 2018: archaic zygomasseteric structure indicates it is better regarded as a stem sciurid. Li et al. 2023 list it among Sciurinae. "Protosciurus" jeffersoni (Emry & Thorington 1982 skeleton) is now Douglassciurus.
notes.material: Cranial and dental material: holotype of P. condoni a nearly complete skull and right mandible; other species based on mandible/maxilla fragments with teeth. No postcranial skeleton referred to Protosciurus s.str. in the sources retrieved (the 1982 skeleton belongs to Douglassciurus jeffersoni).
notes.gliding_evidence: None. Known from skulls/jaws/teeth; dentition of tree-squirrel type (Black 1963); no postcranial evidence of gliding.

locality.details: USA: Oregon (John Day Fm; type of P. condoni), Nebraska (Meng Ranch, type of P. mengi), South Dakota, Wyoming, California (Tecuya Canyon), Texas, Florida; Canada: Saskatchewan - PBDB.
